title: The Iwakura Mission round the world, 1871–73
summary: Meiji Japan's embassy to the treaty powers: the ambassador Iwakura Tomomi, four vice-ambassadors and a party of some fifty officials and scholars, with students, left Yokohama on 23 December 1871 on the SS America. They crossed the United States by rail to Washington, sailed to Liverpool in August 1872, toured Britain, saw Queen Victoria at Windsor on 5 December, then France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Prussia, Denmark, Sweden, Austria, Italy and Switzerland, and came home by Egypt, Aden, Ceylon, Singapore, Saigon, Hong Kong and Shanghai, reaching Yokohama on 13 September 1873. Kume Kunitake wrote the official record. The Continental tour is not drawn, for the article gives its countries and no order, nor is the way from Europe to Egypt.

legs.source: Iwakura Mission (Wikipedia): sailed from Yokohama on the SS America and reached San Francisco on 15 January 1872; the track between is the usual great-circle-ish steamer route, not a logged one
Iwakura Mission (Wikipedia): by train through Salt Lake City and Chicago to Washington, reached 29 February 1872; the line joins those named towns
Iwakura Mission (Wikipedia): school and industrial tours of Boston, New York and Washington, then sailed for the UK in August 1872; the port of sailing is not named in the article
legs.doubt: The article does not say which port they sailed from; New York is the likeliest and is drawn. The Boston tours are not drawn.

legs.source: Iwakura Mission (Wikipedia): arrived at Liverpool on 17 August 1872 on the Cunard steamer Olympus; the track is the usual North Atlantic steamer route
Iwakura Mission (Wikipedia): Liverpool, then Manchester, then London from late August; the groups later split across Britain and are not drawn
Iwakura Mission (Wikipedia): left for France on 16 December 1872 and met President Thiers on 26 December; the Channel crossing is drawn as a straight link, not a track
Iwakura Mission (Wikipedia): the way home went by Egypt, Aden, Ceylon, Singapore, Saigon, Hong Kong and Shanghai; no dates are given for the ports
legs.doubt: The article names only Egypt; Suez is the port from which the Red Sea leg would start. How they reached Egypt from Europe is not given.

legs.source: Iwakura Mission (Wikipedia): Aden, then Ceylon; the article names the island, not a port
Iwakura Mission (Wikipedia): Singapore, Saigon, Hong Kong; Saigon lies up its river, so the line stands off its mouth
legs.doubt: The article names Saigon between Singapore and Hong Kong; the line passes off Cap Saint-Jacques at the river mouth, not up the river.

legs.source: Iwakura Mission (Wikipedia): Hong Kong, Shanghai, then Yokohama, reached on 13 September 1873

events.label: Audience with Queen Victoria at Windsor
events.text: The mission was received by the Queen at Windsor Castle on 5 December 1872, and by the Prince of Wales at Sandringham four days later.
